To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the drug release from PS-coated microcapsules of a drug-resin complex was prolonged and independent of the dissolution media.
polystyrene microcapsules of diltiazam-resin complex were prepared by oil-in-water (O/W) emulsion-solent evaporation method.
the PS-coated microcapsules of diltiazen-resin complex can achieve prolonged release of dltiazem-HCl in the simulated gastric and intestinal fluids.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the preparation of PS-coated microcapsules of diltiazema-Indion 254 complex and the in vitro evaluation of their release characteristics.
the preparation and in vitro evaluation (in simulated gastric and intestinal fluids) of polystyrenecoated microcapsules of diltiazemdiltiazem-resins.
the preparation and characterization of PS-coated microcapsules of diltiazen-resin complex and their evaluation in vitro.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the microcapsules of the drug-resin complex with a PS coat could provide a prolonged drug-release pattern independent of the pH and the presence of digestive enzymes in the dissolution medium.

the PS-coated diltizaem-resin complex prepared by the oil-in-water emulsification-solvent evapolation method could be a suitable dosage form for the controlled release of diltizaem in simulated gastric and/or intestinal fluid.

the drug release from PS-coated microcapsules of diltiazen-resin complex was prolonged for different time intervals depending on the formulation and processing parameters, and was independent of the pH.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PS-coated microcapsules containing diltiazem-Indion 254 complex could be a useful dosage form for sustained release of diltizaem-HCl.

the PS coating of diltiazen-resin complex microcapsules is suitable to achieve prolonged release of the drug in simulated gastric and small intestinal fluid, and the retardation is dependent on the formulation parameters.
the drug-resin complex is suitable for microencapsulation by the oil-in-water emulsification-solvent evapsulation method.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a PS coat on the microcapsules of the diltiazem-Indion 254 complex could provide prolonged release of drug independent of pH.
a simple oil-in-water emulsification-solvent evapolation method can be employed to coat the drug-resin complex to achieve the desired drug-release pattern.
the microcapsules of the drug-resin complex prepared with PS as a coating material are suitable for achieving prolonged release in the simulated gastric and intestinal fluids.
